fullCitation: Eldjarn GH, et al. Large-scale plasma proteomics comparisons through genetics and disease associations. Nature. 2023.
sampleSize: 54,219 UK Biobank (Olink) and 35,892 Icelanders (SomaScan); 1,514 Icelanders measured on both
keyFindings: Compared Olink Explore 3072 in UK Biobank with SomaScan v4 in Iceland; 1,514 Icelanders were measured on both.
A cis-pQTL was found for a similar number of assays on each platform (2,101 Olink, 2,120 SomaScan), but for a larger share of Olink assays (72% vs 43%).
Modest cross-platform correlation: median Spearman 0.33 across 1,848 proteins in the 1,514 Icelanders measured on both.

63% of SomaScan trans-pQTL associations involved a variant associated with more than 10 proteins, vs 52% for Olink; 28% of SomaScan proteins with any pQTL had only such non-specific trans-pQTLs, vs 8% on Olink.
The choice of platform can change conclusions in disease studies (examples: heart failure, Alzheimer's disease, inflammatory bowel disease); the differences at times give useful complementarity.

fullCitation: Katz DH, et al. Proteomic profiling platforms head to head: leveraging genetics and clinical traits to compare aptamer- and antibody-based methods. Science Advances. 2022.
sampleSize: 787 measured on both platforms: 568 Jackson Heart Study, 219 HERITAGE
keyFindings: Compared Olink Explore with SomaScan 1.3K and 5K on precision, accuracy, breadth and phenotypic associations in 568 Jackson Heart Study and 219 HERITAGE participants.
Modest cross-platform correlation for shared targets: median Spearman 0.44 with SomaScan 1.3K, 0.35 with SomaScan 5K.
Olink gave more phenotypic associations, including among overlapping proteins; SomaScan gave more reproducible measurements and greater breadth.
Cis-pQTLs supported more Olink reagents than SomaScan 1.3K reagents: 40% vs 28% at P < 1×10⁻⁵, 25% vs 16% at genome-wide significance.

fullCitation: Kirsher DY, Chand S, Phong A, Nguyen B, Szoke BG, Ahadi S. Current landscape of plasma proteomics from technical innovations to biological insights and biomarker discovery. Communications Chemistry. 2025;8:279.
sampleSize: 78 plasma donors (40 aged, 38 young), measured on all eight platforms
keyFindings: Direct comparison of eight platforms on plasma from the same 78 donors: SomaScan 11K and 7K, Olink Explore HT and 3072, NULISA, Seer Proteograph XT, Biognosys TrueDiscovery and SureQuant targeted MS.
SomaScan achieved best precision (median CV 5.3% for 11K, 5.8% for 7K).
Olink Explore HT median CV ~26.8%; Seer ~26.4%; Biognosys ~29.8%

Agreement varied by pair: SomaScan 11K vs 7K 0.79; Olink HT vs 3072 0.74; NULISA vs Olink 0.75 to 0.79; the highest affinity-to-MS correlation was 0.62 (Olink 3072 vs targeted MS). Per-protein correlations were often bimodal.
Platform choice should be driven by study-specific priorities

Supplementary Data 8 (MS-HAP Depletion arm) provides the Atlas's Biognosys TrueDiscovery protein list, 3,575 proteins by primary UniProt accession, a matched-cohort depletion-workflow list used from v2.8 in place of the earlier PQ500 spectral-library list

fullCitation: Rooney MR, et al. Comparison of proteomic measurements across platforms in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study. Clinical Chemistry. 2023.
sampleSize: 427 ARIC participants measured on both platforms
keyFindings: Comparison in 427 ARIC participants at visit 5 (2011 to 2013).
SomaScan v4 vs Olink Proseek head-to-head on the same samples: 417 protein comparisons (366 unique proteins).
Average cross-platform correlation r = 0.46 (range -0.21 to 0.97); 19% of pairs had r ≥ 0.8.
About half of proteins showed good or modest correlation and half poor; the authors advise that study design account for this variation protein by protein.
disclosureNote: Disclosure: SomaLogic ran SomaScan on ARIC samples at no charge under a collaboration agreement with Johns Hopkins, and one author is a scientific advisor to SomaLogic.

fullCitation: Rooney MR, et al. Correlations within and between highly multiplexed proteomic assays of human plasma. Clinical Chemistry. 2025;71:677-687.
sampleSize: 102 ARIC participants measured on both platforms
keyFindings: Precision of SomaScan 11k and Olink Explore HT in split plasma samples from 102 ARIC participants: median CV 6.8% and 35.7%.

Cross-platform correlations for 4,443 overlapping proteins peaked near r = 0 and r = 0.8, and one-tenth of pairs had r ≥ 0.8. The median was 0.14, below the 0.33 reported for earlier platform versions.
Olink Explore HT precision tracks detectability (r = -0.77 with percent of samples above the limit of detection); its median CV falls to 13.3% when below-LOD values are set to half the LOD.
Precision of the two platforms has diverged as coverage has increased.
disclosureNote: Disclosure: SomaLogic provided the assays at no cost and had no control over design or analysis; one author served on its scientific advisory committee in 2022-2023.

fullCitation: Haslam DE, et al. Stability and reproducibility of proteomic profiles in epidemiological studies: comparing the Olink and SOMAscan platforms. Proteomics. 2022.
sampleSize: 104 participants across four Olink experiments; 53 of them also on SomaScan (14 delayed-processing, 39 sampled one year apart)
keyFindings: Compared stability and reproducibility of Olink (972 proteins) and SOMAscan 7K (6,596 proteins) in archived plasma.
Both platforms showed reproducibility in archived plasma and stability after delayed processing; over 90% of assays were stable (ICC or r ≥ 0.40) in samples collected a year apart.
With processing delayed by up to 48 hours, more Olink than SOMAscan assays stayed stable: 55% vs 44% at ICC or r ≥ 0.75, 87% vs 72% at ≥ 0.40.
Among 817 proteins on both platforms, correlations were high (r > 0.75) for 14.7% and poor (r < 0.40) for 44.8%.

fullCitation: Pietzner M, et al. Nanoparticle-enriched mass spectrometry proteomics in British South Asians identifies links between genetic variants, plasma protein levels and disease risk. Nature Genetics. 2026;58:1866-1876.
sampleSize: 1,464 Genes & Health participants; 1,396 measured on all three platforms
keyFindings: Compared nanoparticle-enriched MS (Seer Proteograph XT) with SomaLogic 11k and Olink Explore HT in British South Asian participants; 1,396 were measured on all three.
Seer detected 8,079 protein groups at least once, 5,768 of them in at least 70% of samples.
Showed the potential of MS-based proteomics for pQTL discovery in non-European ancestries: over 1,200 locus-protein associations, more than half not previously reported.

About one-third of the protein groups detected were not captured by the affinity platforms. Protein-altering variants mapped to 38.8% of MS cis-pQTLs, and peptide-level evidence helped clarify genetic mechanisms.
Multiple platforms are needed to capture the full spectrum of pQTLs. Most disagreement between platforms was technical (54 to 67% explained by technical factors).

fullCitation: Feng W, et al. NULISA: a proteomic liquid biopsy platform with attomolar sensitivity and high multiplexing. Nature Communications. 2023;14:7238.
sampleSize: 151 samples from 79 healthy donors and 72 patients (assay validation)
keyFindings: Attomolar-level sensitivity: limit of detection 10 aM (0.24 fg/mL) for HIV p24 in plasma.
Dual capture-and-release mechanism suppresses assay background, improving proximity ligation sensitivity about 10,000-fold.
200-plex panel was more sensitive than a proximity extension assay (Olink Explore) for low-abundance biomarkers in patients with autoimmune diseases and COVID-19.
195 of 204 targets were detected in more than half of 151 samples (79 healthy donors, 72 patients).

fullCitation: Dagher M, et al. nELISA: a high-throughput, high-plex platform enables quantitative profiling of the inflammatory secretome. Nature Methods. 2025;22:2375-2385.
sampleSize: 7,392 cell-culture samples from PBMCs of 6 donors (assay validation; no participant cohort)
keyFindings: A 191-plex inflammation panel profiled 7,392 PBMC samples, about 1.4 million measurements.
Antibody pairs are preassembled on barcoded beads; in spike-in testing of the 191-plex panel, 5 of more than 36,000 possible noncognate interactions were detected.
1,536 wells per day on one cytometer in 384-well format; 7,392 samples on a 191-plex panel in under one week.
Described as cost-efficient, with reagent savings and cost advantages over MS and sequencing-based platforms. No per-sample price is reported.
Quantification across seven orders of magnitude, with sub-pg/mL sensitivity.

fullCitation: Sissala N, Babačić H, Leo IR, et al. Comparative evaluation of Olink Explore 3072 and mass spectrometry with peptide fractionation for plasma proteomics. Communications Chemistry. 2025;8:327.
sampleSize: 114 patients by mass spectrometry; 88 of them also by Olink
keyFindings: Compared HiRIEF LC-MS/MS with Olink Explore 3072 on 88 plasma samples; 1,129 proteins were measured by both.
Median cross-platform Spearman correlation ρ=0.59 (IQR 0.33–0.75); rises to ρ=0.68 on high-quality subset
Platforms exhibit complementary coverage: Olink stronger at low-abundance targets; MS stronger at mid-to-high abundance
Tier 1 pQTL proteins (Eldjarn confidence tiers) showed higher MS–Olink agreement (ρ=0.71 vs ρ=0.50 for tier 3)
In most cases, MS–Olink correlations here were higher than the Olink–SomaScan correlations reported for matching proteins in earlier studies.
Note: MS method is HiRIEF LC-MS/MS (DDA, TMT-labelled), not Seer Proteograph XT; Olink panel is Explore 3072, not HT

fullCitation: Bahai A, et al. High-throughput plasma proteomic platforms: Insights from a multi-ethnic Asian cohort. bioRxiv. 2025.
sampleSize: 500 PRECISE-SG100K participants on SomaScan; 216 also on Olink, 50 also on Seer
keyFindings: Pilot for planned profiling of all 100,000 PRECISE-SG100K participants: 500 participants on SomaScan 11K, 216 of them also on Olink Explore HT, 50 also on MS-Seer.
Three-platform comparison in a multi-ethnic Asian cohort (Chinese, Indian and Malay).
Protein levels differed between ethnic groups. SomaScan identified more ethnicity-differentiated proteins than Olink, and 191 proteins were robust across datasets.
Limited overlap (1,740 proteins across all three platforms) and modest median correlations (0.10 to 0.34).

fullCitation: Rea Reyes RE, Wilson RE, Langhough RE, et al. Targeted proteomic biomarker profiling using NULISA in a cohort enriched with risk for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Alzheimer's & Dementia. 2025;21:e70166.
sampleSize: 252 plasma samples on the NULISAseq CNS panel; 218 also measured by Simoa p-tau217
keyFindings: NULISAseq p-tau217 classified amyloid and tau PET status with areas under the curve of 0.92 and 0.86.
NULISAseq p-tau217 correlated with Simoa p-tau217 (r = 0.84, n = 218), and the two assays were comparable for amyloid PET, both with areas under the curve above 0.90.
The panel also measures ApoE4 protein, which was raised in amyloid-positive participants; the authors attribute this to the higher prevalence of APOE ε4.
Phosphorylated TDP-43 (pTDP43-409) was raised in impaired participants and correlated with hippocampal volume decline and cognitive trajectories; the authors say this needs replication.

fullCitation: Zeng X, Lafferty TK, Sehrawat A, et al. Multi-analyte proteomic analysis identifies blood-based neuroinflammation, cerebrovascular and synaptic biomarkers in preclinical Alzheimer's disease. Molecular Neurodegeneration. 2024;19:68.
sampleSize: 176 plasma samples from 113 MYHAT-NI participants on the NULISAseq CNS panel; classical biomarkers also measured by Simoa
keyFindings: NULISAseq CNS panel measured 116 plasma biomarkers, with 97.2 ± 13.9% of targets above assay limits of detection.
p-tau217 was the top marker of amyloid PET pathology (AUC 0.930 after adjustment for age, sex and APOE genotype).
Classical Alzheimer's biomarkers correlated significantly with Simoa assays.
Neuroinflammation, synaptic and cerebrovascular proteins showed tau PET-dependent longitudinal changes; the authors say these need further validation.

fullCitation: Suhre K, Chen Q, Halama A, et al. A genome-wide association study of mass spectrometry proteomics using a nanoparticle enrichment platform. Nature Genetics. 2025;57:2987-2996.
sampleSize: 1,260 discovery participants (Tarkin) and 325 replication samples (QMDiab) on the Seer Proteograph
keyFindings: Genome-wide association study of MS proteomics using the Seer Proteograph workflow on a timsTOF Pro 2, reporting 35 previously unreported replicated pQTLs.
Over 30% of previously reported affinity pQTLs evaluated were confirmed by MS as consistent with changes in protein abundance.
Another 30% could not be replicated and are possibly due to epitope effects, though the authors say other explanations need case-by-case consideration.
15.3% of proteins in its pQTLs had a missingness pQTL, and the authors note that nanoparticle-enriched MS is not entirely free of epitope-like effects.

fullCitation: Nicholas JC, Katz DH, Tahir UA, et al. Cross-ancestry comparison of aptamer and antibody protein measures. Nature Communications. 2026;17:1054.
sampleSize: 1,930 MESA participants measured on both SomaScan 7k and Olink Explore 3072
keyFindings: 2,157 proteins measured on both platforms; inter-platform correlations were bimodal (median r = 0.30).
About 25 to 30% of genetic signals on each platform are likely driven by protein-altering variants.
80 proteins correlated differently across ancestry groups, likely in part because protein-altering variant frequencies differ by ancestry.
Adjusting for protein-altering variants with opposite effects by platform improved inter-platform correlation and gave more concordant genetic and phenotypic associations.
